why: rules.yaml records precision evidence per estate under `checked:`. This maps every estate name that may appear there to the language it is written in, so a `checked` entry naming an estate in another language is caught mechanically. Written after exactly that defect: an edit that located a rule's `checked:` block by searching forward from its id found the next such block in the file instead, and gave three never-sampled rules another rule's samples. Real estates are polyglot and the map must say so: the Camel integration estate carries one Python file, the .NET estate eight TypeScript ones, and the Spring Cloud estate a JavaScript front end. Narrower entries made this control cry wolf, which is the failure mode that gets a control switched off.
